puzzles.description: Scrollable system logs. Select the lines containing key data.

lines: [03:41:12] WARN  process.monitor: Unregistered process detected in subnet-private-7a
[03:41:14] ERROR purge.scheduler: Purge sequence armed. T-60:00
[03:41:15] INFO  ec2.status: EC2-unit-47 RUNNING. credentials rotated.
[03:41:17] WARN  route.table: No route to igw. Public subnet isolated.

hints: The logs contain more than warnings. Look at the data values.
Three lines have critical data: a VPC ID, a password hash, and a gateway ID.
Select the lines with vpc-0f8c3a, 6e6574776f726b, and igw-abc123.

puzzles.description: Log into EC2-unit-47 using the password from the system logs

falseOutputs.no_prerequisite: ACCESS DENIED. Credentials unknown. The password was recently rotated — check the system logs.
falseOutputs.wrong_answer: LOGIN FAILED. Invalid password. The hash in the logs might need decoding.

hints: The password was recently changed. Check the system logs in the Spawn Room.
Look for 'password hash' in the logs. The value 6e6574776f726b is hex-encoded.
Use the Hex Decoder tool. 6e6574776f726b in hex = 'network'.

puzzles.description: Search the archive terminal for useful data
hints: The terminal is a search engine. What did the blast door warning say you'd need?
The blast door mentioned a 'Security Group checkpoint'. Search for that.
Type 'security group' into the terminal.

puzzles.description: Overlay the Security Group Blueprint (#125) with the Port Reference Card (#133) to reveal the corrupted port number

config.reveals: The corrupted port on the blueprint aligns with 443 (HTTPS) on the port reference. The scattered line fragments complete the number.

hints: Both cards have alignment marks. What if they were meant to be placed together?
Try overlaying the Security Group Blueprint with the Port Reference Card.
The corrupted port is 443 — HTTPS. You can see it when the cards are combined.

config.message: ...configure... inbound... port four-four-three... secure channel only... outbound... let everything out... repeat... four-four-three inbound... all outbound...

puzzles.description: Configure inbound port and outbound range for the Security Group

config.prompt:
SECURITY GROUP CONFIGURATION

Enter inbound port:

hints: You need info from three sources: the blueprint, the port card, and the speaker.
The inbound port is for secure web traffic. The speaker says 'four-four-three'. Outbound is 'everything' = 0.
Inbound Port: 443. Outbound Port: 0 (all).

puzzles.description: A locked door behind the archive. Enter the 4-digit access code.
hints: Look carefully at the Archive Room description. The vault door keypad is visible.
The keypad beside the vault door displays a faint sequence.
The code is 7143 — shown on the keypad display next to the vault door.

puzzles.description: Configure an IAM policy to authorize gateway transit for EC2 instances
hints: Read the policy console description — it tells you what the policy needs to authorize.
You need to Allow creating a route to the gateway. The action is an EC2 action on route tables.
Effect: Allow. Action: ec2:CreateRoute. Resource: arn:aws:ec2:*:*:route-table/*.

puzzles.description: Configure NACL inbound and outbound rules. Unlike Security Groups, NACLs are stateless — you must allow return traffic explicitly.
hints: Check the NACL Reference Sheet you picked up in the Policy Vault. It has the exact rules.
Inbound: Allow TCP 443, then Deny ALL. Outbound: Allow TCP 1024-65535 (ephemeral ports), then Deny ALL.
Toggle all four rules to match: Inbound 443=Allow, Inbound ALL=Deny, Outbound 1024-65535=Allow, Outbound ALL=Deny.

puzzles.description: Reconnect the severed power cables to restore gateway power. Use the Power Routing Diagram.

falseOutputs: Sparks! Wrong connection. Check the diagram.
No power. The wiring doesn't match the diagram.

hints: You've seen clues about these wires in earlier rooms. Think back — what color was connected to what?
Spawn Room: red cable → Power Core. System Logs: blue → Data Link. Processing Chamber: green → Signal Relay. Network Diagram: yellow → Ground Loop.
Red→Power Core, Blue→Data Link, Green→Signal Relay, Yellow→Ground Loop. Grey is a decoy — leave it unconnected.

puzzles.description: Enter VPC ID, gateway ID, and route to activate the gateway. Each value comes from a different card.
hints: The console needs three values. You've seen each one on a different card from your journey.
VPC ID is in the system logs. Gateway ID is on the communicator. The route CIDR is on the network diagram.
VPC ID: vpc-0f8c3a. Gateway ID: igw-abc123. Route CIDR: 10.0.1.0/24.
